purpose: Declared model routing. Task class -> tier, agent template -> task class, observed session -> task class. Read by bin/heimdall-tier (declaration + conformance) and bin/lib/tier_audit.py (drift audit). Changing a tier here changes what the audit calls drift, so this file is the single place the routing decision lives.
no_pinned_ids: Tiers are BARE ALIASES on purpose. Claude Code resolves opus|sonnet|haiku to the current generation of that tier; a pinned full model id in an operational path silently ages (that is how Opus 5 shipped while Heimdall kept spawning claude-opus-4-8). Pin only for bench/eval reproducibility, via HEIMDALL_MODEL_<TIER>. model_id_tier_patterns below classify OBSERVED history and are therefore version-free regexes, not pins.
tier_price_rule: A tier states no price: it is priced at the newest model_prices row whose family is the tier name (a bare alias resolves to the current generation). Add a row and the tier price follows; bin/heimdall-tier derives it and fails loudly for a tier with no row.

inherit_declaration.meaning: A spawn template may declare `tier: inherit` instead of a tier. It pins NO model and runs on whatever Claude Code default the operator chose for their own session. Used by agents/heimdall.md, the main orchestrator, per owner directive: hmd does not override the model the human picked.
inherit_declaration.not_a_tier: It deliberately has no entry under `tiers` — no rank and no price. Ranking it would let a deferral be read as an escalation or a cut, and pricing it would invent a number nobody can verify. bin/heimdall-tier keeps it out of the delta arithmetic entirely.
inherit_declaration.still_enforced: The gate's invariant is unchanged — the declaration must equal what executes. For `inherit` that is cross-checked POSITIVELY against the same `model:` field every other template uses: Claude Code's agent-file parser accepts the literal `model: inherit` (verified in the shipped 2.1.227 binary), so deference is stated, not inferred from silence. An omitted `model:` is still accepted because it executes identically, but it is weaker evidence — silence cannot be told apart from a forgotten field. Naming any OTHER model alongside `tier: inherit` is two claims at once and fails. On a security_sensitive class it additionally requires a `tier_reason:`, because the operator's default could sit below what the class requires and that has to be an owned decision rather than silent drift.

rank_note: fable shares opus's rank because spec 2.1 writes the top row as 'Opus / Fable' — either satisfies that class, so an opus-class task seen on fable is not tier drift. Fable's extra cost is governed by the ZDR policy gate and the weekly allowance, not by the drift rank.

long_context_premium.note: The per-tier prices (tier_price_rule) are BASE rates for requests at or under 200K input tokens (haiku: 100K, see its long_context card). Only sonnet's opt-in [1m] is confirmed to carry a long-context premium above that threshold. opus does NOT carry it: Anthropic's own model docs state opus's 1M window bills at standard API pricing with no long-context premium, and this repo's own token-spend-forensics.md prices opus sessions past 900K input tokens at flat base rate plus only the ordinary cache multipliers, never a premium term, so a base-rate total from this table IS the bill on opus while on sonnet[1m] it is only a FLOOR. fable is undocumented either way and must not be assumed to match opus or sonnet until measured. bin/heimdall-model-resolve appends [1m] to sonnet (where 1M is opt-in) and leaves opus/fable bare (1M is already their default maximum); haiku has no [1m] alias (none ships in Claude Code 2.1.331), so the suffix never applies to it, although Haiku 5.5's own window is 1M (Haiku 4.5's was 200K) and it bills a second rate card above 100K prompt tokens (its long_context card).
long_context_premium.why_not_priced_here: The exact premium multiplier is set by the API's pricing, not by hmd, and hardcoding a number here would create a second cost accounting that can silently disagree with the first. This block records WHERE the premium applies so a reader is never misled into treating a base-rate total as complete; it deliberately does not invent the multiplier.

cache_price_multipliers.note: Every cache WRITE is a fixed multiple of the model's own input price, identical across haiku/sonnet/opus/fable and across every generation model_prices lists. A cache READ is this multiple only by default: a model_prices row overrides it where the list price deviates (Fable 5.1 and 5.2 read at 0.025x, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 at 0.05x). bin/heimdall-cost-forensics is the consumer: it derives each model's cache lines from these multipliers instead of storing them per row.

model_prices.purpose: Per-model list prices in US dollars per million tokens, read by bin/heimdall-cost-forensics to price a session transcript, and through bin/lib/hmd_model_prices.py by bin/heimdall-tokens (the cost it derives) and bin/lib/fg_agent.py (the Study A spend meter). This is the one place a rate is written (tier prices derive from it). One price per tier cannot price a transcript, because one tier's generations list at different prices (Opus 5.5 below Opus 5, Haiku 5.5 at a tenth of Haiku 4.5) and a rate wrong by a factor reads as a number, which is worse than an unpriced token. Rows are matched on family + version, kept as separate fields so this file names no model id (test/operational-model-pin.test.sh forbids a pinned id on this path).
model_prices.source: claude-api skill model reference. Rows through Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5, Opus 5 and Haiku 4.5: pricing cached 2026-06-24. Claude 5.5 generation (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku), Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2: pricing cached 2026-11-03 (SKILL.md Current Models table; shared/models.md; shared/prompt-caching.md Economics; shared/model-migration.md, Migrating to Claude Haiku 5.5). Opus 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5: the published prices evals/benchmark/false-green/PREREG.md Amendment 1 recorded on 2026-10-05, when the Study A spend meter still held a table of its own; the same reference (shared/models.md, 2026-11-03) lists Opus 4.5 as a legacy model that is still active and Sonnet 4.5 as deprecated, retiring 2026-11-30.
model_prices.rate_rules: A row gives input and output. Cache writes are cache_price_multipliers x input. cache_read is cache_price_multipliers.cache_read x input unless the row sets it: Fable 5.1, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 read at 0.025x, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 at 0.05x. A row may set cache_read to null when the read price is unconfirmed: that slice is reported as unpriced, never guessed. long_context is a second rate card for a request whose prompt (uncached input + cache reads + cache writes) is above above_prompt_tokens; Haiku 5.5 bills $0.10 in / $0.50 out up to 100K prompt tokens and $0.50 / $2.50 above, its cache lines following each card's own input rate. Not modelled: fast mode, which bills a premium multiple of the same card (those requests read low), and non-first-party platforms, which price separately.
model_prices.unlisted_versions: A version NEWER than every listed version of its family is priced as the newest listed one and reported as an ESTIMATE, so a new generation is never silently unpriced. A family this table lacks, or an older version it does not list, is never priced: an older model's price cannot be inferred from a newer one's. Add a row to make an estimate exact.

rows.note: cache_read was unconfirmed when this row was written (pricing cached 2026-06-24), so that slice is reported as unpriced. The 2026-11-03 model reference lists Mythos 5.1 reads at $0.25/MTok; set it to 0.25 together with the partial-pricing fixture in test/heimdall-cost-forensics.test.sh, which relies on this null.

non_zdr_note: Claude Fable 5 requires 30-day data retention; a zero-data-retention org gets 400 invalid_request_error on every Fable request. Selection is therefore deny-by-default and must fail LOUDLY — a silent downgrade to a cheaper tier would hide the fact that a repo cannot run this tier at all.

hook.summary: Hook bodies: fires per event, bounded input, decision is a classification not a design.

classifier.summary: Label a bounded input against a fixed set of categories.

formatter.summary: Lint, format, rename, mechanical rewrite with a deterministic oracle.

janitor.summary: Janitor and reaper tasks: sweep stale state, close orphans, prune logs.

marker_check.summary: Presence/absence checks for markers, sentinels and required fields.

coder.summary: Standard coder agents: implement to a stated scope with tests.

test_writer.summary: Write and run tests against an existing implementation.

doc.summary: Documentation agents: write and sync prose against shipped behaviour.

triage.summary: Triage: read signals, group them, decide what deserves escalation.

orchestrator.summary: Decompose work, spawn and supervise agents, hold the plan.
orchestrator.no_downgrade_reason: The orchestrator decides which gates run at all. Weakening it weakens every gate downstream of it.

architecture.summary: Architecture and design reasoning; decisions that outlive the session.
architecture.tier_note: Set to opus at this table's 2026-08-08 creation, before CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-11 model-routing directive made sonnet the default coding tier and closed the opus exception list to exactly reviewer/verifier/security-auditor. This entry was stale drift, not a deliberate carve-out: architecture work carries no security_sensitive flag and no no_downgrade_reason (unlike orchestrator/security_critical/gate_adjudication, which do), so it was never meant to be a protected floor.

security_critical.summary: Security-critical reasoning: threat modelling, vulnerability assessment, dependency and secret audit.
security_critical.no_downgrade_reason: A cheaper check that misses a vulnerability costs far more than the whole $57.73 this table was built to recover. If the spend is unacceptable, reduce FREQUENCY — never the tier.

gate_adjudication.summary: Adjudicating a gate: review, verification, deciding whether evidence actually proves the claim.
gate_adjudication.no_downgrade_reason: A gate that passes work it should have failed is worse than no gate, because it manufactures false confidence.

forensics.summary: Incident and spend forensics: reconstruct what happened from evidence.
forensics.tier_note: Set to opus at this table's 2026-08-08 creation, before CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-11 model-routing directive made sonnet the default coding tier and closed the opus exception list to exactly reviewer/verifier/security-auditor. This entry was stale drift, not a deliberate carve-out: forensics carries no security_sensitive flag and no no_downgrade_reason (unlike orchestrator/security_critical/gate_adjudication, which do), so it was never meant to be a protected floor.
